tier_reason: Lowered A to C (vpxyz/xorshift precedent: measured code carries a correctness bug in its hot path). The enricher's code reading shows RuneWidth returns 2 for every code point in U+2600-27BF and in U+1F300-1F5FF, U+1F680-1F6FF and U+1F900-1F9FF, although per go-runewidth v0.0.19's Unicode 15.1 tables 402 of the 448 code points in U+2600-27BF and 259 in those SMP blocks are not East Asian Wide (for example the common terminal symbols check mark, cross, right arrowhead, star and heart); the table generator filters these ranges out and the tests repeat the same ranges, so they cannot catch it. The CI 'TUI Prompt' row (156.0 versus 270.7 versus 389.7 ns) therefore times a wrong answer (17 for the prompt string where go-runewidth gives 16). The inputs of the catalogued ASCII, CJK, emoji, flag and ZWJ rows are unaffected, but a drop-in that returns different widths from the baseline is not doing the same work, and the harness remains first-party on a shared runner with 10-20% variance.

corrections.caveats: Correctness bug in the hot path: RuneWidth reports width 2 for all of U+2600-27BF and the U+1F300-1F5FF, U+1F680-1F6FF and U+1F900-1F9FF blocks, where most code points are not East Asian Wide (402 of 448 in U+2600-27BF per go-runewidth's Unicode 15.1 tables), so common terminal symbols measure wrong and the CI 'TUI Prompt' row times a wrong answer (17 versus go-runewidth's 16); the generator filters these ranges and the tests cannot catch it. The *WithOptions path lacks ZWJ, variation-selector and flag handling (a family emoji measures 8) and returns len(s) for ASCII (control characters count 1); WithEmojiPresentation is never read; no Truncate, Wrap or Fill. First-party CI numbers on a shared GitHub Actions runner (-count=3, -benchtime=100ms) that the workflow itself calls directional with 10-20% variance. The work differs: go-runewidth v0.0.19 runs full UAX #29 grapheme segmentation on every string while uniwidth uses a SWAR ASCII path and a lightweight state machine; Unicode tables differ (16.0 versus 15.1).
